The search for ""mycreativeshop.com/developers/rich-text" OR "mycreativeshop" "rich-text" konva" returned the following summary:
This is a reference to **Rich Text for Canvas by MyCreativeShop**, a specialized developer library designed to solve the long-standing challenge of adding editable, multi-styled rich text directly onto HTML canvas elements and **Konva.js** stages[1][2].

### Key Features of `@mycreativeshop/rich-text` / `@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva`

* **Native Konva Integration:** Rather than relying on hacky HTML overlays (`foreignObject` or DOM inputs), text boxes act as native Konva nodes (`RichText`) that you can add to a stage or layer like any other shape[1].
* **Advanced Text Styling:** Supports mixed fonts, sizes, colors, weights, bullet/numbered lists, character/paragraph styles, tab stops, shadows, outlines, and even curved text within a single text box[3][4].
* **Built-in Editing UX:** Includes cursor management, text selection, keyboard navigation, copy/paste with styles, undo/redo functionality, resize handles, and spellcheck[3].
* **Precise Vector Rendering:** Uses a WebAssembly module (`harfbuzzjs`) to draw letters as vector shapes straight from font files, ensuring text looks identical across all browsers and matches print output precisely[3][5].
* **Upgrading Legacy Konva Apps:** Provides utility functions like `convertKonvaTextToRichText()` to seamlessly migrate existing `Konva.Text` instances over to the rich text engine without breaking app logic or custom attributes[6].

### Basic Usage with Konva

```javascript
import { enableRichText, RichText, createDocumentFromText } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva";
import Konva from "konva";

const stage = new Konva.Stage({ container: 'container', width: 800, height: 600 });
const layer = new Konva.Layer();
stage.add(layer);

// Turn on editing for the Konva stage
const rt = enableRichText(stage);

// Add a rich text node to the layer
layer.add(new RichText({
  x: 40,
  y: 40,
  width: 400,
  draggable: true,
  document: createDocumentFromText("Grand opening", 48),
}));
```

### Licensing
The library is free to use during local development (displaying a subtle "Development" watermark on text boxes without a key), while production deployment requires a paid site license[1][5].

1: # Playground
2: 
3: Rich Text for Canvas has no toolbar of its own: your app keeps its own buttons and menus, in its own design, and each
4: control calls one formatting command. This page wires a small toolbar (font, size, bold, italic, underline,
5: strikethrough, color, bullets, numbers, alignment, undo and redo) to the library, as the demo's Playground does. The
6: pages linked at the end cover each group of commands in full.
7: 
8: ## What a command changes
9: 
10: Every formatting command works on the current selection:
11: 
12: | When | The command changes |
13: | --- | --- |
14: | A box is being edited and words are selected | The selected words |
15: | A box is being edited and only the cursor shows | The cursor's paragraph |
16: | A box is selected but not being edited | All of the box's text |
17: | You pass boxes as the last argument | All of the text in those boxes |
18: | No box is selected | Nothing |
19: 
20: Each command is one undo step, even when it changes several boxes; commands on the same box less than a second apart
21: join one step. Commands are on `rt.manager` on Konva and on `rt` on a plain canvas, with the same names:
22: 
23: ```ts
24: // Konva
25: const rt = enableRichText(stage);
26: rt.manager.toggleBold();
27: rt.manager.toggleBold([headline, footer]); // these boxes, whatever is selected
28: 
29: // Plain canvas
30: const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render });
31: rt.toggleBold();
32: ```
33: 
34: ## Build the toolbar
35: 
36: The toolbar is plain HTML in your page:
37: 
38: ```html
39: <div id="toolbar">
40:   <select id="font"><option>Poppins</option><option>Lora</option><option>Oswald</option></select>
41:   <select id="size"><option>14</option><option>18</option><option>24</option><option>36</option><option>48</option></select>
42:   <button id="bold">B</button>
43:   <button id="italic">I</button>
44:   <button id="underline">U</button>
45:   <button id="strike">S</button>
46:   <input id="color" type="color">
47:   <button id="bullets">Bullets</button>
48:   <button id="numbers">Numbers</button>
49:   <button data-align="left">Left</button>
50:   <button data-align="center">Center</button>
51:   <button data-align="right">Right</button>
52:   <button data-align="justify">Justify</button>
53:   <button id="undo">Undo</button>
54:   <button id="redo">Redo</button>
55: </div>
56: ```
57: 
58: ## Connect each control to a command
59: 
60: The same code serves both surfaces: only the first line differs.
61: 
62: ```ts
63: const commands = rt.manager; // on a plain canvas: const commands = rt;
64: const byId = <T extends HTMLElement>(id: string) => document.getElementById(id) as T;
65: 
66: const font = byId<HTMLSelectElement>("font");
67: font.onchange = async () => {
68:   await commands.setFontFamily(font.value); // loads the font first, then applies it
69:   font.blur();
70: };
71: 
72: const size = byId<HTMLSelectElement>("size");
73: size.onchange = () => {
74:   commands.setFontSize(Number(size.value));
75:   size.blur();
76: };
77: 
78: byId("bold").onclick = () => commands.toggleBold();
79: byId("italic").onclick = () => commands.toggleItalic();
80: byId("underline").onclick = () => commands.toggleUnderline();
81: byId("strike").onclick = () => commands.toggleStrikethrough();
82: 
83: const color = byId<HTMLInputElement>("color");
84: color.onchange = () => {
85:   commands.setColor(color.value);
86:   color.blur();
87: };
88: 
89: for (const button of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>("[data-align]")) {
90:   button.onclick = () => commands.setAlignment(button.dataset.align as "left" | "center" | "right" | "justify");
91: }
92: 
93: byId("undo").onclick = () => commands.undo();
94: byId("redo").onclick = () => commands.redo();
95: ```
96: 
97: `setFontFamily` returns a promise. The box keeps showing its current font while the new one downloads, and the promise
98: resolves once the text is drawn in the new font. Any [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com) family works with no
99: setup; see [Fonts](fonts) for your own.
100: 
101: ## Keep typing after a toolbar click
102: 
103: While someone types in a box, keys are heard on the window. The library leaves keys alone while the page's focus is in
104: an `input`, `textarea`, `select` or `contenteditable` element, so typing after choosing from a menu would go to the
105: menu. That is why the menus above call `blur()` after a change.
106: 
107: Buttons do not take keys, but a click moves the page's focus to the button. To keep focus where it was, prevent the
108: default on `mousedown`:
109: 
110: ```ts
111: const toolbar = byId("toolbar");
112: toolbar.addEventListener("mousedown", (e) => {
113:   if ((e.target as HTMLElement).closest("button")) e.preventDefault();
114: });
115: ```
116: 
117: A click on your toolbar does not end editing on either surface: editing ends on a press on the canvas outside the box
118: being edited, or with Esc.
119: 
120: ## Show the current formatting
121: 
122: `onFormattingChange` reports what the selection looks like every time it changes: the font, size and styles, the
123: color, the alignment, the list, and whether undo and redo can do anything. Your callback is called once right away, and
124: with `null` when nothing is selected.
125: 
126: ```ts
127: import { defaultRichTextContext, type FormattingState } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva";
128: 
129: let current: FormattingState | null = null;
130: 
131: defaultRichTextContext.onFormattingChange((state) => {
132:   current = state;
133:   byId("bold").classList.toggle("active", !!state?.bold);
134:   byId("italic").classList.toggle("active", !!state?.italic);
135:   font.value = state?.fontFamily ?? "";
136:   size.value = state ? String(Math.round(state.fontSize)) : "";
137:   byId<HTMLButtonElement>("undo").disabled = !state?.canUndo;
138:   byId<HTMLButtonElement>("redo").disabled = !state?.canRedo;
139: });
140: // Plain canvas: rt.onFormattingChange((state) => { ... })
141: ```
142: 
143: [Your own toolbar](toolbar) lists every field of the report and how a full toolbar uses it.
144: 
145: ## Bullets and numbers
146: 
147: `toggleBulletList(style)` turns a list on or off for the reached paragraphs, and `setBulletStyle(style)` changes the
148: marker of paragraphs that are already list items. `"disc"` is a bullet and `"decimal"` numbers the items 1. 2. 3. With
149: the report above, one Bullets button and one Numbers button behave as people expect: a second press turns the list
150: off, and pressing the other button switches the marker.
151: 
152: ```ts
153: function list(style: "disc" | "decimal") {
154:   const numbered = current?.listStyle === "decimal";
155:   if (current?.isList && numbered === (style === "decimal")) commands.toggleBulletList(); // the same button: off
156:   else if (current?.isList) commands.setBulletStyle(style); // the other button: switch the marker
157:   else commands.toggleBulletList(style); // not a list yet: on
158: }
159: 
160: byId("bullets").onclick = () => list("disc");
161: byId("numbers").onclick = () => list("decimal");
162: ```
163: 
164: [Lists](lists) covers every marker, including any character and shapes.
165: 
166: ## Undo and redo
167: 
168: `undo()` and `redo()` step through the same history as Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z (Cmd on a Mac), which work while a box
169: is being edited. Typing, each toolbar command and resizing a box with its handles are steps. To put text changes in
170: your app's own
171: undo history instead, see [Your app's undo](history).
172: 
173: ## More commands
174: 
175: | Page | Commands |
176: | --- | --- |
177: | [Character styles](characters) | `setFontFamily`, `setFontSize`, `scaleFontSize`, `setFontWeight`, `setColor`, `toggleBold`, `toggleItalic`, `toggleUnderline`, `toggleStrikethrough` |
178: | [Paragraphs](paragraphs) | `setAlignment`, `setLineHeight`, `setLetterSpacing`, `setParagraphSpacing` |
179: | [Lists](lists) | `toggleBulletList`, `setBulletStyle` |
180: | [Tab stops](tabs) | `setTabStops` |
181: | [Your own toolbar](toolbar) | `onFormattingChange`, `getFormattingState` |
182: | [Keyboard and mouse](editing) | `copy`, `cut`, `paste`, `undo`, `redo` |
183:

1: # Your own toolbar
2: 
3: Rich Text for Canvas has no toolbar of its own. Your app keeps its own buttons, menus and panels, in its own design.
4: The library reports what the selected text looks like every time that changes, and each of your controls sends one
5: command, such as `toggleBold()` or `setFontSize(24)`, to the selected box or to the selected words.
6: 
7: ## Keep your controls in step with the selection
8: 
9: Listen with `onFormattingChange`. On Konva the listener belongs to the context, the editing session the stage's
10: manager is part of; on a plain canvas it is on the object `createCanvasRichText` returns.
11: 
12: ```ts
13: // Konva
14: import { defaultRichTextContext } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva";
15: 
16: const stop = defaultRichTextContext.onFormattingChange((f, box) => {
17:   if (!f) return toolbar.disable(); // nothing is selected
18:   toolbar.enable();
19:   fontMenu.value = f.fontFamily;
20:   boldButton.classList.toggle("active", f.bold);
21:   undoButton.disabled = !f.canUndo;
22: });
23: 
24: // Plain canvas
25: rt.onFormattingChange((f, box) => { /* the same */ });
26: ```
27: 
28: - The callback receives the formatting and the box it describes. Both are `null` when no text box is selected.
29: - It is called once right away with the latest report, so your toolbar shows the current formatting from the start.
30: - It is called again after every command, when the cursor moves or the selection changes, when a box is selected or
31:   deselected, and after undo and redo. A report identical to the one before is not sent again.
32: - It returns a function that stops listening.
33: 
34: On Konva, `defaultRichTextContext` is the context of every stage enabled without one. If you created your own context
35: with [createRichTextContext](ref:createRichTextContext), for example for [your app's undo](history), listen on that
36: context instead. `rt.manager.context` is the manager's context in either case:
37: 
38: ```ts
39: rt.manager.context.onFormattingChange((f) => updateToolbar(f));
40: ```
41: 
42: ## Read the formatting when you need it
43: 
44: `getFormattingState()` returns the same report on demand: from `rt.manager.getFormattingState()` on Konva, or
45: `rt.getFormattingState()` on a plain canvas. It returns `null` when no box is being edited or selected. Pass a box to
46: read that box instead: `rt.manager.getFormattingState(box)`.
47: 
48: ## What the report describes
49: 
50: - **While a box is being edited:** the formatting the next letter typed would take. With words selected, that is the
51:   first selected letter; with only a cursor, the letter before the cursor. Paragraph fields come from the cursor's
52:   paragraph.
53: - **When a box is selected but not being edited:** its first visible letter and that letter's paragraph.
54: - **A box with no text:** the default formatting.
55: 
56: > **Note:** A selection that mixes styles is reported by its first letter. There is no "mixed" value, so a Bold button
57: > shows the first letter's bold. `toggleBold()` follows what the report shows: when `bold` is `true` it removes bold
58: > from all of the selection, otherwise it makes all of it bold. The other toggles work the same way.
59: 
60: ## Every field
61: 
62: | Field | What it holds |
63: | --- | --- |
64: | `fontFamily` | The font family name. |
65: | `fontSize` | The size in pixels, as it looks on screen (see the tip below). |
66: | `fontWeight` | The numeric weight, 100 to 900, when the text sets one. `undefined` when it sets none: show the weight `bold` implies. |
67: | `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strikethrough` | `true` when that style is on. |
68: | `color` | The letters' color, as a CSS color string. |
69: | `strokeWidth` | The outline's width in pixels, as it looks on screen. `0` means no outline. |
70: | `strokeColor` | The outline's color. |
71: | `alignment` | The paragraph's alignment: `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"` or `"justify"`. |
72: | `lineHeight` | The paragraph's line height, as a multiple of the font size. |
73: | `letterSpacing` | The paragraph's letter spacing, in pixels as it looks on screen. |
74: | `paragraphSpacing` | The space after the paragraph, as a multiple of its font size. |
75: | `tabStops` | The paragraph's tab stops, or an empty array when it has none. See [Tab stops](tabs). |
76: | `isList` | `true` when the paragraph is a list item. |
77: | `listType` | `"bullet"` for a list item, unless the document marks it `listType: "number"`. `undefined` for a paragraph. |
78: | `listStyle` | The list item's marker: `"disc"`, `"circle"`, `"square"`, `"decimal"` (1. 2. 3.) or a character. `undefined` for a paragraph. |
79: | `hasSelection` | `true` when words are selected in the box being edited, and `false` with only a cursor. |
80: | `selectionLength` | How many characters are selected. An emoji counts as one. |
81: | `cursorIndex` | The cursor's position, as a character index in the box. `0` when the box is not being edited. |
82: | `canUndo`, `canRedo` | Whether the library's history has a step to undo or redo. |
83: 
84: > **Tip:** Inside a scaled Konva group, `fontSize`, `strokeWidth` and `letterSpacing` are reported and set as they look
85: > on screen. A value read, changed by 2 and written back moves by exactly 2.
86: 
87: ## Connect each kind of control
88: 
89: Each control reads one field of the report and sends one command. On Konva the commands are on `rt.manager`; on a
90: plain canvas they are on `rt`. The names are the same. First the report, shown on every control:
91: 
92: ```ts
93: let state: FormattingState | null = null;
94: rt.manager.context.onFormattingChange((f) => { // plain canvas: rt.onFormattingChange
95:   state = f;
96:   for (const control of toolbar.controls) control.disabled = !f;
97:   if (!f) return;
98: 
99:   fontMenu.value = f.fontFamily;
100:   sizeField.value = String(Math.round(f.fontSize));
101:   weightMenu.value = String(f.fontWeight ?? (f.bold ? 700 : 400));
102:   boldButton.classList.toggle("active", f.bold);
103:   italicButton.classList.toggle("active", f.italic);
104:   underlineButton.classList.toggle("active", f.underline);
105:   colorInput.value = f.color;
106:   for (const button of alignButtons) button.classList.toggle("active", button.dataset.align === f.alignment);
107:   lineHeightMenu.value = String(f.lineHeight);
108:   bulletsButton.classList.toggle("active", f.isList && f.listStyle !== "decimal");
109:   numbersButton.classList.toggle("active", f.isList && f.listStyle === "decimal");
110:   undoButton.disabled = !f.canUndo;
111:   redoButton.disabled = !f.canRedo;
112: 
113:   // A selection note
114:   selectionNote.textContent = f.hasSelection
115:     ? `${f.selectionLength} characters selected`
116:     : `Cursor at ${f.cursorIndex}`;
117: });
118: ```
119: 
120: Then one command per control:
121: 
122: ```ts
123: const cmd = rt.manager; // plain canvas: const cmd = rt;
124: 
125: // Menus and fields: a value in
126: fontMenu.onchange = () => cmd.setFontFamily(fontMenu.value); // loads the font first; returns a promise
127: sizeField.onchange = () => cmd.setFontSize(Number(sizeField.value));
128: weightMenu.onchange = () => cmd.setFontWeight(Number(weightMenu.value));
129: lineHeightMenu.onchange = () => cmd.setLineHeight(Number(lineHeightMenu.value)); // 1.2 is 120%
130: 
131: // Toggles
132: boldButton.onclick = () => cmd.toggleBold();
133: italicButton.onclick = () => cmd.toggleItalic();
134: underlineButton.onclick = () => cmd.toggleUnderline();
135: 
136: // Color: any CSS color string
137: colorInput.oninput = () => cmd.setColor(colorInput.value);
138: 
139: // Alignment: one button per value
140: for (const button of alignButtons) button.onclick = () => cmd.setAlignment(button.dataset.align as "left" | "center" | "right" | "justify");
141: 
142: // Lists: on, off, or from bullets to numbers
143: function listButton(style: string) {
144:   const on = state?.isList && (state.listStyle === "decimal") === (style === "decimal");
145:   if (on) cmd.toggleBulletList(); // off
146:   else if (state?.isList) cmd.setBulletStyle(style);
147:   else cmd.toggleBulletList(style);
148: }
149: bulletsButton.onclick = () => listButton("disc");
150: numbersButton.onclick = () => listButton("decimal");
151: 
152: // Undo and redo
153: undoButton.onclick = () => cmd.undo();
154: redoButton.onclick = () => cmd.redo();
155: ```
156: 
157: `toggleBulletList` makes the reached paragraphs list items, or paragraphs again when all of them are list items
158: already. To tell a numbered list from bullets, read `listStyle`: `"decimal"` is numbered. [Lists](lists) shows every
159: marker, and [Character styles](characters) and [Paragraphs](paragraphs) list every command.
160: 
161: ## Keep the selection while people use the toolbar
162: 
163: A click on your toolbar should leave the keyboard focus where it was, so people can format some words and go on typing:
164: 
165: - **Buttons:** call `preventDefault()` on the button's `mousedown`. The button then does not take the keyboard focus,
166:   and the keys people type keep going to the text.
167: - **Menus and fields:** the library leaves the keys alone while the focus is in an input, a textarea, a select or an
168:   element with `contenteditable`, so people can type a font size during editing. After the value is applied, call
169:   `blur()` on the field so the next keys go back to the text.
170: 
171: ```ts
172: toolbar.addEventListener("mousedown", (e) => {
173:   if ((e.target as HTMLElement).closest("button")) e.preventDefault();
174: });
175: sizeField.addEventListener("change", () => {
176:   rt.manager.setFontSize(Number(sizeField.value));
177:   sizeField.blur();
178: });
179: ```
180: 
181: ## Where a command lands
182: 
183: - **While a box is being edited:** on the selected words. With only a cursor and no selection, on the cursor's whole
184:   paragraph.
185: - **When a box is selected but not being edited:** on all of its text.
186: - **On boxes you name:** pass them as the last argument. Each named box is changed the same way: the box being edited
187:   through its selection or cursor, any other box in all of its text.
188: 
189: ```ts
190: rt.manager.toggleBold([headline, subhead]);
191: rt.manager.setFontSize(24, [headline, subhead]);
192: rt.manager.toggleBulletList("disc", [list]);
193: // Plain canvas: rt.toggleBold([headline, subhead])
194: ```
195: 
196: Paragraph settings (alignment, line height, letter spacing, paragraph spacing, tab stops and lists) always change
197: whole paragraphs: every paragraph the selection touches. While [Story Mode](story) is open, commands reach the words
198: selected in its panel.
199: 
200: Each command is one undo step, even when it changes several boxes. `setFontFamily(family, boxes, options)` takes the
201: boxes before the options, on both surfaces; [Character styles](characters) describes the options.
202: 
203: ## Undo and redo buttons
204: 
205: `rt.manager.undo()` and `rt.manager.redo()` on Konva, `rt.undo()` and `rt.redo()` on a plain canvas, step through the
206: library's history. Enable the buttons from `canUndo` and `canRedo` in the report.
207: 
208: > **Note:** In "host" history mode your app keeps the undo steps, so `canUndo` and `canRedo` are always `false` and
209: > the library's `undo()` and `redo()` do nothing. Enable your buttons from your own history instead. See
210: > [Your app's undo](history).
211:

216: - [defaultRichTextContext](ref:defaultRichTextContext)
217: - [RichTextManager.getFormattingState](ref:TextFormatting.getFormattingState)
218: - [CanvasRichText.onFormattingChange](ref:CanvasRichText.onFormattingChange)
219: - [CanvasRichText](ref:CanvasRichText)

1: # Getting started
2: 
3: Rich Text for Canvas adds editable rich text to an HTML canvas: a cursor, selection, keyboard navigation, copy and
4: paste with styles, undo, spellcheck, lists, tab stops, curved text, fills and shadows. Letters are drawn as shapes from
5: the font file, so every browser draws the same pixels and print matches the screen. The library works on a
6: [Konva](https://konvajs.org) stage or on a plain `<canvas>` with no canvas library. This page installs the library,
7: adds your license key and puts a first text box on each surface.
8: 
9: ## Install
10: 
11: ```bash
12: npm install @mycreativeshop/rich-text
13: ```
14: 
15: An app built on [Konva](https://konvajs.org) installs Konva (version 10) beside it:
16: 
17: ```bash
18: npm install @mycreativeshop/rich-text konva
19: ```
20: 
21: | Import from | For |
22: | --- | --- |
23: | `@mycreativeshop/rich-text` | Apps that draw their own `<canvas>`, with no Konva |
24: | `@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva` | Apps built on Konva |
25: 
26: The package includes TypeScript types.
27: 
28: ### Vite settings
29: 
30: The text engine is a WebAssembly module (`harfbuzzjs`) that loads with a top-level `await`. With Vite, leave it out of
31: dependency pre-bundling and build for ES2022:
32: 
33: ```js
34: // vite.config.js
35: export default defineConfig({
36:   optimizeDeps: {
37:     exclude: ["harfbuzzjs"],
38:     esbuildOptions: { target: "es2022" },
39:   },
40:   build: { target: "es2022" },
41: });
42: ```
43: 
44: If the module can't load, the console shows `[rich-text:text-engine] harfbuzzjs FAILED to load` and text is measured
45: by the browser instead, so line breaks can differ from print.
46: 
47: ## Install with a script tag
48: 
49: A page with no bundler can load the browser build from jsDelivr. The browser build is a set of ES modules, so load it
50: with `<script type="module">`. Replace `1.0.1` with the version you use.
51: 
52: ```html
53: <script type="module">
54:   import { configureRichText, createCanvasRichText, createDocumentFromText } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mycreativeshop/rich-text@1.0.1/dist/browser/index.js";
55: </script>
56: ```
57: 
58: For Konva, load Konva first with its own script tag. The library uses the page's global `Konva`.
59: 
60: ```html
61: <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/konva@10/konva.min.js"></script>
62: <script type="module">
63:   import { configureRichText, enableRichText, RichText } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mycreativeshop/rich-text@1.0.1/dist/browser/konva.js";
64: </script>
65: ```
66: 
67: The browser build has the plain-canvas entry (`index.js`) and the Konva entry (`konva.js`).
68: 
69: ## Add your license key
70: 
71: Copy your key from your licenses page and set it once, before you create text boxes:
72: 
73: ```ts
74: import { configureRichText } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text"; // on Konva: "@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva"
75: 
76: configureRichText({ licenseKey: "rt1.…" });
77: ```
78: 
79: Everything works without a key. Each text box then shows a watermark across its text:
80: 
81: - **Development**, faint, on localhost, on IP addresses, on test names (`.localhost`, `.local`, `.test`, `.example`,
82:   `.invalid`), on pages opened from a file, and on any domain that is not on your license, such as a staging site.
83: - **Unlicensed**, larger and red, on any other site with no valid key, or when a license has ended.
84: 
85: The watermark is drawn over the text, inside each box, and is in exported images too. It never changes how text lays
86: out. Add your production domains on your licenses page to remove it on those domains. A domain with an underscore (`my_shop.example.com`) can't be added; use a
87: domain without one.
88: 
89: The key is checked against your domains in the browser. When a check is due, the library also asks our license server,
90: in the background, whether the license is still active. That request sends only your license id, the page's domain
91: and the library version. If our server can't be reached, nothing changes on your pages.
92: 
93: ## Konva or a plain canvas
94: 
95: The same text engine, layout and drawing run behind both entry points, so a document looks identical on either. Pick
96: by what your app already draws with.
97: 
98: | | Konva | Plain canvas |
99: | --- | --- | --- |
100: | Import from | `@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva` | `@mycreativeshop/rich-text` |
101: | Turn it on | `const rt = enableRichText(stage)` | `const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render })` |
102: | A text box is | a Konva node, [RichText](ref:RichText) | a [CanvasTextBox](ref:CanvasTextBox) that your render paints |
103: | Selection and handles | your own `Konva.Transformer` | built in (turn them off with `objectControls: false`) |
104: | Pointer events | Konva's, heard by the library | yours, forwarded to `rt` |
105: | Formatting commands | on `rt.manager` | on `rt` |
106: 
107: Formatting commands have the same names on both surfaces (`toggleBold`, `setFontSize`, `setColor` and the rest), and
108: documents move between them unchanged. Keys and paste are heard on the window on both surfaces while a box is being
109: edited.
110: 
111: ## Your first text box on Konva
112: 
113: ```ts
114: import Konva from "konva";
115: import { configureRichText, createDocumentFromText, enableRichText, RichText } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva";
116: 
117: configureRichText({ licenseKey: "rt1.…" });
118: 
119: const stage = new Konva.Stage({ container: "editor", width: 800, height: 600 });
120: const layer = new Konva.Layer();
121: stage.add(layer);
122: 
123: // Editing, the cursor, keys, clipboard, spellcheck and undo for every text box on the stage
124: const rt = enableRichText(stage);
125: 
126: layer.add(new RichText({ x: 40, y: 40, width: 400, draggable: true, document: createDocumentFromText("Grand opening", 48) }));
127: 
128: // Your selection: put the clicked box on your transformer
129: const selection = new Konva.Transformer();
130: layer.add(selection);
131: stage.on("mousedown touchstart", (e) => {
132:   if (e.target instanceof RichText) selection.nodes([e.target]);
133:   else if (e.target === stage) selection.nodes([]);
134: });
135: ```
136: 
137: [enableRichText](ref:enableRichText) watches the stage. Any [RichText](ref:RichText) you add, to a layer or inside a
138: group, can be selected and edited, and a box you remove is released. The stage needs a layer before you call
139: `enableRichText`; the text uses the stage's first layer unless you pass `{ layer }`. Selection follows your own
140: transformer: when you set its nodes, the library sees the change, so your app keeps its usual click-to-select.
141: 
142: Click a box to select it, and click it again to place the cursor and type. `createDocumentFromText(text, fontSize,
143: fontFamily, color)` makes one paragraph per line of `text`; the font defaults to Poppins.
144: 
145: ## Your first text box on a plain canvas
146: 
147: ```ts
148: import { configureRichText, createCanvasRichText, createDocumentFromText } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text";
149: 
150: configureRichText({ licenseKey: "rt1.…" });

Created At: 2026-10-27T23:17:14+08:00
Completed At: 2026-10-27T23:17:15+08:00

1: # Curved text
2: 
3: Curved text sets a box's words along an arc: bent up over a headline, bent down under one, or around a circle on a
4: round badge or seal. People edit curved text like any other text. The box lies flat while it is being edited and
5: curves again when editing ends.
6: 
7: > **Note:** Curved text is marked experimental in this version of the library: its commands and settings may change
8: > in a later version.
9: 
10: ## Bend a box's text
11: 
12: From your toolbar, for the selected box:
13: 
14: ```ts
15: // Konva: const rt = enableRichText(stage)
16: rt.manager.setCurveAmount(120); // degrees of arc; turns the curve on
17: rt.manager.toggleCurve(); // curved or flat again
18: 
19: // Plain canvas: const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render })
20: rt.setCurveAmount(120);
21: rt.toggleCurve();
22: ```
23: 
24: The amount is in degrees of arc, from -360 to 360. A positive amount bends the text up, so it sits on top of a circle;
25: a negative amount bends it down, so it hangs from the bottom of one. `180` is a half circle. `setCurveAmount` also turns
26: the curve on, and a curve turned on with `toggleCurve` starts at 180.
27: 
28: A curve belongs to the whole box, never to a selection. To change boxes you name instead of the selected box, pass them
29: as the optional last argument: `rt.manager.setCurveAmount(120, [topLine])`. Each call is one undo step.
30: 
31: ## Bend a box you hold
32: 
33: A text box has the same settings as methods, for setting up a design in code:
34: 
35: ```ts
36: topLine.setCurveEnabled(true);
37: topLine.setCurveAmount(120);
38: 
39: topLine.getCurveEnabled(); // true
40: topLine.getCurveAmount(); // 120
41: ```
42: 
43: These methods are the same on a Konva [RichText](ref:RichText) and a plain-canvas [CanvasTextBox](ref:CanvasTextBox).
44: They lay the box out and redraw it at once, and they are not undo steps: use the toolbar commands above for changes
45: people should be able to undo.
46: 
47: ## How a curved box behaves
48: 
49: - **One line.** Every letter in the box goes along the same arc. Use one box for each curved line.
50: - **The box fits the arc.** Turning the curve on remembers the box's width, and the box is then sized to the curved
51:   text. Turning the curve off gives the box its remembered width back.
52: - **Handles.** A curved box has only corner handles, and they scale the text. A side handle would change the width,
53:   which doesn't change a curve. A curved box inside a Konva group has no handles of its own: the group's handles scale
54:   it.
55: - **Editing.** The box lies flat while someone types in it, with the usual cursor and selection, and curves again when
56:   editing ends.
57: - **Effects.** A drop shadow follows the curved letters, and a gradient or image fill shows on them. See
58:   [Shadows and outlines](effects) and [Gradient and image fills](fills).
59: - **Loading.** A curved box shows nothing until its fonts have loaded, instead of a faint flat preview.
60: 
61: ## Text around a circle
62: 
63: To set text on a circle of an exact size, such as the ring of a round seal, give the box an `arcRadius` instead of an
64: amount. The library works out the bend from the words' own width, so the letters' baselines sit on that circle. Pass
65: the settings as `documentCurve` when you create the box:
66: 
67: ```ts
68: // Konva
69: layer.add(
70:   new RichText({
71:     x: 0, y: 0, width: 300, document: createDocumentFromText("FRESH BAKED DAILY", 28),
72:     documentCurve: { enabled: true, amount: 180, arcRadius: 108, side: "top", centerX: 150, centerY: 150 },
73:   })
74: );
75: 
76: // Plain canvas
77: rt.addBox({
78:   x: 0, y: 0, width: 300, document: createDocumentFromText("SINCE 1998", 28),
79:   documentCurve: { enabled: true, amount: 180, arcRadius: 108, side: "bottom", centerX: 150, centerY: 150 },
80: });
81: ```
82: 
83: | Field | What it does |
84: | --- | --- |
85: | `enabled` | Whether the text is drawn curved. |
86: | `amount` | The bend in degrees, from -360 to 360. Ignored when `arcRadius` is set. |
87: | `arcRadius` | The radius of the circle the text sits on, in pixels. The bend comes from the words' width. |
88: | `side` | With `arcRadius`: `"top"` (the default) runs along the top of the circle and bends up; `"bottom"` runs along the bottom, bends down and reads left to right. |
89: | `centerX`, `centerY` | With `arcRadius`: the circle's center, in the same coordinates as the box's `x` and `y`. Give both. |
90: 
91: With a center, the library moves the box when it is first laid out so its arc sits on that circle. After that the box
92: can be dragged like any other. When people type more or fewer words, the box moves so the line stays on its circle,
93: centered. With `arcRadius` set, `getCurveAmount()` returns the bend the words take on the circle.
94: 
95: A curve is a setting of the box, not of its document: `getDocument()` does not include it. On Konva it is saved with
96: the node's attributes (`node.toObject()`) and can be changed with `box.setAttr("documentCurve", curve)`. On a plain
97: canvas, read it from `box.attrs.documentCurve` and pass it back to `addBox` when you load the design. Undo and redo
98: include the curve.
99: 
100: ## Older text

1: # Shadows and outlines
2: 
3: A drop shadow and an outline make text stand out from a busy background. Together with the letters' color they make
4: looks such as a sticker, a retro offset or a neon glow. The text stays editable with any of them. The library blurs
5: the shadow itself instead of leaving it to the browser, so a shadow looks the same in every browser and in an export.
6: 
7: ## Add a drop shadow
8: 
9: ```ts
10: // Konva: const rt = enableRichText(stage)
11: rt.manager.setShadow({ color: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)", offsetX: 3, offsetY: 4, blur: 8 });
12: rt.manager.setShadow(null); // remove it
13: 
14: // Plain canvas: const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render })
15: rt.setShadow({ color: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)", offsetX: 3, offsetY: 4, blur: 8 });
16: ```
17: 
18: | Field | What it does |
19: | --- | --- |
20: | `color` | The shadow's color, any CSS color. Use `rgba()` to make it see-through: the alpha is the shadow's opacity. |
21: | `offsetX` | How far the shadow moves right, in pixels. A negative value moves it left. |
22: | `offsetY` | How far the shadow moves down, in pixels. A negative value moves it up. |
23: | `blur` | The blur radius in pixels, as in CSS `text-shadow`. `0` is a hard-edged shadow. |
24: 
25: The shadow belongs to the whole box, not to a selection: `setShadow` changes the shadow of every box it reaches, even
26: while some words are selected. To change boxes you name instead of the selected box, pass them as the optional last
27: argument: `rt.manager.setShadow(shadow, [headline])`. Each call is one undo step.
28: 
29: The shadow follows the shapes that are drawn: the letters with their outlines, underlines, list markers and curves. It
30: stays visible while the text is edited. When the type is scaled, by a corner handle or by `scaleFontSize` on a box that
31: is not being edited, the shadow's offsets and blur scale with it. A shadow changes only how the text is drawn, never
32: where lines break.
33: 
34: To show the current shadow in your controls, read it from the box's document: `box.getDocument().shadow` is the shadow,
35: or `undefined` when the box has none.
36: 
37: ## Add an outline
38: 
39: ```ts
40: rt.manager.setStrokeWidth(3); // pixels; 0 removes the outline
41: rt.manager.setStrokeColor("#FF7903"); // any CSS color
42: ```
43: 
44: An outline is a character style, unlike the shadow: it changes the selected words while someone edits the box, or all
45: of the box's text when the box is only selected, like the other [character styles](characters). If none of those
46: letters has an outline color yet, `setStrokeWidth` uses black. The outline color shows only where the outline width is
47: above 0.
48: 
49: The outline is drawn behind the letters, so it never covers their color: only the part of the outline outside each
50: letter shows. Inside a scaled Konva group, the width is read and set in pixels as it looks on screen.
51: 
52: ## Combine them into a look
53: 
54: A look is three settings: the letters' color, an outline and a shadow. These recipes are the ones in the live demo.
55: Each takes the font size, `f`, so the outline and shadow keep their proportions at any size. Each command is its own
56: undo step.
57: 
58: ```ts
59: // Drop shadow: a soft shadow straight below the letters
60: function dropShadow(f: number) {
61:   rt.manager.setColor("#5E2DC1");
62:   rt.manager.setStrokeWidth(0);
63:   rt.manager.setShadow({ color: "rgba(27, 17, 48, 0.3)", offsetX: 0, offsetY: 0.05 * f, blur: 0.1 * f });
64: }
65: 
66: // Sticker: orange letters in a thick dark outline, on a small soft shadow
67: function sticker(f: number) {
68:   rt.manager.setColor("#FF7903");
69:   rt.manager.setStrokeColor("#1B1130");
70:   rt.manager.setStrokeWidth(0.18 * f);
71:   rt.manager.setShadow({ color: "rgba(27, 17, 48, 0.3)", offsetX: 0.035 * f, offsetY: 0.035 * f, blur: 0.02 * f });
72: }
73: 
74: // Neon: light letters in a purple outline, with a purple glow all around
75: function neon(f: number) {
76:   rt.manager.setColor("#8661D0");
77:   rt.manager.setStrokeColor("#5E2DC1");
78:   rt.manager.setStrokeWidth(0.09 * f);
79:   rt.manager.setShadow({ color: "#5E2DC1", offsetX: 0, offsetY: 0, blur: 0.12 * f });
80: }
81: ```
82: 
83: The demo's other looks use the same three settings:
84: 
85: | Look | Color | Outline | Shadow |
86: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
87: | Hard shadow | Purple | None | Orange, offset down and right by 0.05 x the font size, no blur |
88: | Outline | Purple | Orange, 0.04 x the font size | None |
89: | Retro | Orange | The background's color, 0.07 x the font size | Purple, offset down and right by 0.07 x the font size, no blur |
90: | Glow | Purple | None | Orange, no offset, blur 0.12 x the font size |
91: 
92: A glow is a shadow with no offset and a blur. An outline in the background's color, under an offset shadow, separates
93: the letters from their shadow.
94: 
95: ## In the document
96: 
97: The shadow is saved as the document's `shadow`. Outlines are saved on runs of text as `strokeColor` and `strokeWidth`.
98: 
99: ```json
100: {

1: # Gradient and image fills
2: 
3: A fill paints a text box's letters with a two-color gradient or with an image, such as a photo or a texture, instead of
4: their own colors. The text stays editable, and the fill stays in place as people type.
5: 
6: ## Fill with a gradient
7: 
8: ```ts
9: // Konva: const rt = enableRichText(stage)
10: rt.manager.setFill({ type: "gradient", color1: "#5E2DC1", color2: "#FF7903", angle: 90 });
11: 
12: // Plain canvas: const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render })
13: rt.setFill({ type: "gradient", color1: "#5E2DC1", color2: "#FF7903", angle: 90 });
14: ```
15: 
16: | Field | What it does |
17: | --- | --- |
18: | `type` | `"gradient"`. |
19: | `color1` | The color the gradient starts with, any CSS color. |
20: | `color2` | The color the gradient ends with, any CSS color. |
21: | `angle` | The direction in degrees, as in CSS `linear-gradient`: `0` runs from `color1` at the bottom to `color2` at the top, `90` from left to right, `180` from top to bottom. |
22: 
23: The gradient runs across the whole box, not across each letter, so the letters together show one gradient.
24: 
25: ## Fill with an image
26: 
27: ```ts
28: rt.manager.setFill({ type: "image", url: "https://images.example.com/beach.jpg", fit: "cover" });
29: ```
30: 
31: | Field | What it does |
32: | --- | --- |
33: | `type` | `"image"`. |
34: | `url` | The image's address. |
35: | `fit` | How the image is placed in the box. `"cover"` (the default) scales the image to fill the box, centered, and crops what falls outside it. `"contain"` scales the whole image to fit inside the box, centered, so part of the box can be left without image. `"stretch"` stretches the image to the box's width and height. |
36: 
37: The image is placed against the whole box. Until the image has loaded, the letters show their own colors, then the box
38: redraws with the image. On Konva, [cloneStageForExport](ref:cloneStageForExport) waits for fill images before it
39: draws, so an export shows them.
40: 
41: > **Note:** The library loads the image as a cross-origin request. An image on another domain must be served with an
42: > `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header that allows your page. Without one the image does not load, and the letters
43: > keep their own colors. The library tries each failed address once per page load.
44: 
45: ## Remove a fill
46: 
47: ```ts
48: rt.manager.setFill(null); // the letters' own colors again
49: rt.manager.setColor("#1B1130"); // a solid color also removes the fill
50: ```
51: 
52: The letters' own colors are kept under a fill, so removing the fill shows them again. Setting a color with `setColor`
53: removes the fill from the whole box, even when only some words are selected.
54: 
55: ## What a fill covers
56: 
57: A fill belongs to the whole box, not to a selection: `setFill` changes the box while some words are selected too. To
58: change boxes you name instead of the selected box, pass them as the optional last argument:
59: `rt.manager.setFill(fill, [headline])`. Each call is one undo step.
60: 
61: Under a fill:
62: 
63: - Every letter is painted with the fill, including bold, italic and outlined letters. The outline keeps its own color.
64: - Underlines, strikethroughs and tab leaders are painted with the fill.
65: - Character list markers (a bullet, a number, a symbol) are painted with the fill. A vector marker keeps its own
66:   colors.
67: - A drop shadow is cast by the filled letters, as it is by plain letters.
68: - [Curved text](curved) shows the fill, a gradient or an image.
69: 
70: A fill changes only how the text is drawn, never where lines break.
71: 
72: ## Older text
73: 
74: A document records the text version it was made with (see [JSON documents](document)). In text version 1, curved text
75: under an image fill is drawn in the letters' own colors, and underlines and strikethroughs keep the run's color under
76: any fill. New documents use the latest version.
77: 
78: ## In the document
79: 
80: The fill is saved as the document's `fill`, so it is saved, copied and undone with the text. A document you build
81: yourself can carry one before it is loaded:
82: 
83: ```ts
84: const doc = createDocumentFromText("Summer sale", 72);
85: doc.fill = { type: "gradient", color1: "#5E2DC1", color2: "#FF7903", angle: 90 };
86: box.setDocument(doc);
87: ```
88: 
89: ## In the API reference
90: 
91: - [TextFill](ref:TextFill), [GradientFill](ref:GradientFill) and [ImageFill](ref:ImageFill)
92: - [TextFormatting](ref:TextFormatting): `setFill`, `setColor`
93: - [RichTextDocument](ref:RichTextDocument): `fill`

1: # Shrink to fit
2: 
3: A design often gives text a fixed space: a headline band 128 pixels high, a name line on a badge. When the words change,
4: `copyfitDocument` makes the type smaller, only as far as it must, so every word fits the box's width and the height you
5: give. Font sizes, outline widths, letter spacing and the shadow scale together, so the text keeps its look.
6: 
7: ## Fit new words into a box
8: 
9: Build the new document at the text's full design size, then hand it to the box with the height it must fit:
10: 
11: ```ts
12: // The new words at the headline's own size, 40px
13: const next = createDocumentFromText(words, 40, "Playfair Display");
14: 
15: // Made smaller only as far as it must, to fit 128 pixels high
16: const scale = headline.copyfitDocument(next, { containerHeight: 128 });
17: // scale: the factor applied to the sizes - 0.75 means the 40px words are now 30px
18: ```
19: 
20: `copyfitDocument` is a method of every text box: the Konva `RichText` and the plain-canvas `CanvasTextBox`. It
21: replaces the box's document with the fitted one, keeps the box's width, and is one undo step. It returns the scale it
22: applied to the document's sizes.
23: 
24: Copyfit only shrinks. To let shorter words grow back, start from the full-size document each time, as above. The scale
25: it finds is within 1% of the largest one that fits (the `tolerance` option).
26: 
27: > **Note:** Without `containerHeight`, only the width is checked: copyfit makes sure no word is wider than the box. A
28: > box's own height always grows to fit its text, so it cannot be the limit.
29: 
30: ### Options
31: 
32: | Option | Default | Does |
33: | --- | --- | --- |
34: | `containerHeight` | none | The height the text must fit in, in pixels |
35: | `containerWidth` | the box's width | The width to fit to. The box is set to this width. |
36: | `minScale` | `0.1` | The smallest scale allowed, as a multiple of the document's sizes (`0.5` is half size). The text never goes below it, even if it then overflows. |
37: | `maxIterations` | `20` | The most trial layouts the search makes |
38: | `tolerance` | `0.01` | The search stops once the scale is known to within this fraction |
39: 
40: To keep text legible, express a minimum size as a scale:
41: 
42: ```ts
43: headline.copyfitDocument(next, { containerHeight: 128, minScale: 12 / 40 }); // never below 12px
44: ```
45: 
46: Copyfit measures with the fonts already loaded. If the new document uses a family that is not on the page yet, load it
47: first so the fit is measured in the real font:
48: 
49: ```ts
50: await loadFonts(next);
51: headline.copyfitDocument(next, { containerHeight: 128 });
52: ```
53: 
54: ## Fit when a box loads
55: 
56: The `copyfit` setting shrinks a box's text once, when its fonts have loaded:
57: 
58: ```ts
59: // Konva
60: new RichText({ x: 28, y: 32, width: 352, document: doc, copyfit: { enabled: true, containerHeight: 128, minFontSize: 12 } });
61: 
62: // Plain canvas
63: rt.addBox({ x: 28, y: 32, width: 352, document: doc, copyfit: { enabled: true, containerHeight: 128, minFontSize: 12 } });
64: ```
65: 
66: | Field | Does |
67: | --- | --- |
68: | `enabled` | Turns the fit on |
69: | `containerHeight` | The height to fit in. On Konva, when it is left out, the box's `height` setting is used. A canvas box has no height setting, so set it there. |
70: | `minFontSize` | The smallest size to shrink to. If the text cannot fit at that size, it shrinks further, because fitting comes first. |
71: | `maxFontSize` | Lets the text grow, up to this size for its largest letters, to fill the height. Without it, text only shrinks. |
72: | `newText` | New words for a design made with other words: the box lays out its original text, takes the height that text needs as the space to fill, and fits `newText` into it. Each line becomes a paragraph in the look of the paragraph it replaces; extra lines take the first paragraph's look. |
73: 
74: The fitted sizes are written into the document, and the `copyfit` setting is then removed from the box, so a saved
75: design does not fit again each time it opens. A box being edited is not fitted.
76: 
77: ## Scale a document yourself
78: 
79: [scaleDocumentTypography](ref:scaleDocumentTypography) returns a copy of a document with its type scaled: font sizes,
80: letter spacing, border widths, outline widths, the base size and the shadow. Line height, paragraph spacing and list
81: indents are multiples of the font size, so they stay as they are.
82: 
83: ```ts
84: import { scaleDocumentTypography } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva";
85: 
86: const half = scaleDocumentTypography(doc, 0.5);
87: ```
88: 
89: It is exported from the Konva entry point, `@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva`.
90: 
91: ## Check whether text fits
92: 
93: `layoutAt(document, width)` lays a document out the way a box would - its fonts, its fallback size - and returns the
94: result without changing the box:
95: 
96: ```ts
97: const trial = headline.layoutAt(next, headline.width());
98: if (trial.height > 128) showWarning("The headline is too long for its space");
99: ```

1: # Fonts
2: 
3: Every [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com) family works with no setup: a box loads the faces its text uses when it
4: appears, and `setFontFamily("Pacifico")` loads Pacifico before applying it. Your own fonts, and fonts your users upload,
5: take one setting: a lookup that tells the library where a family's files are.
6: 
7: ## How loading works
8: 
9: - A box shows its own words faintly in a stand-in font while its fonts download, then draws them in the real font. It
10:   never shows a blank box or a spinner.
11: - Each face is measured from the font file itself, so line breaks are the same in every browser and in print.
12: - Along with the faces a box uses, the library loads each family's regular, bold, italic and bold italic faces, so Bold
13:   and Italic in your toolbar draw the real face at once.
14: - A face that fails to download is retried automatically. Until it arrives, its text draws in a stand-in font and the
15:   box shows a warning mark, described below.
16: 
17: ## Change the font
18: 
19: ```ts
20: // Konva
21: await rt.manager.setFontFamily("Playfair Display");
22: 
23: // Plain canvas
24: await rt.setFontFamily("Playfair Display");
25: ```
26: 
27: `setFontFamily` loads the family first, then applies it, and the promise resolves with the text already laid out in
28: the new font. Until then the box keeps its current font. Bold, italic and weight are kept. Like every formatting
29: command, it changes the selected text while a box is being edited, or the whole box when it is only selected, or the
30: boxes you pass: `setFontFamily("Oswald", [title])`.
31: 
32: ## Your own fonts
33: 
34: Tell the library where a family lives with a lookup. The lookup is asked each time a family is met, so fonts your app
35: learns about later, such as an upload, are found without calling `configureRichText` again.
36: 
37: ```ts
38: import { configureRichText } from "@mycreativeshop/rich-text"; // on Konva: "@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva"
39: 
40: configureRichText({
41:   fonts: {
42:     lookup: (family) => {
43:       if (family === "Brand Serif") {
44:         return { files: [{ weight: 400, url: "/fonts/brand.woff2" }, { weight: 700, url: "/fonts/brand-bold.woff2" }] };
45:       }
46:       if (family === "Acme Sans") return { fontFaceUrl: "https://cdn.example.com/acme-sans.css" };
47:       return undefined; // a Google family, or one you know nothing about
48:     },
49:   },
50: });
51: ```
52: 
53: The lookup returns a [FontInfo](ref:FontInfo) for a family, or nothing:
54: 
55: | Field | Is |
56: | --- | --- |
57: | `files` | The family's font files, one per face: `{ weight, style, url }` or `{ weight, style, bytes }`. Any of .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .otf. Used before `fontFaceUrl`. |
58: | `fontFaceUrl` | A stylesheet with the family's `@font-face` rules |
59: | `weights` | The weights the family ships, so a weight it lacks resolves to one it has |
60: 
61: A file's `weight` defaults to 400 and its `style` to `"normal"`. A weight the family lacks is drawn from the nearest face
62: it has; the library never makes a fake bold. Return nothing for a family you know nothing about. If the lookup throws,
63: the family is loaded as if there were no lookup.
64: 
65: > **Note:** The library reads font files itself, to measure them. A font on another origin must be served with an
66: > `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header that allows your page.
67: 
68: When text uses one of your fonts, its address is recorded in the document (`fontMetadata`), with the weights it ships
69: (a stylesheet font's `weights`; files carry their own). The design then opens anywhere, such as a print server or
70: another app, without your lookup, and draws the same weights there. Files given as `bytes` have no address: a design
71: that uses them names the family only, and opens where your lookup knows it.
72: 
73: ### Fonts your users upload
74: 
75: Give the lookup the uploaded file, as an object URL or as bytes:
76: 
77: ```ts
78: const uploaded = new Map<string, string>(); // family -> object URL
79: 
80: configureRichText({
81:   fonts: { lookup: (family) => (uploaded.has(family) ? { files: [{ url: uploaded.get(family) }] } : undefined) },
82: });
83: 
84: input.onchange = async () => {
85:   const file = input.files![0];
86:   const family = file.name.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "");
87:   uploaded.set(family, URL.createObjectURL(file)); // a file with no weight draws at 400
88:   await rt.manager.setFontFamily(family); // plain canvas: rt.setFontFamily(family)
89: };
90: ```
91: 
92: An object URL works only in the page that made it, and it is recorded in the document like any address. To keep a
93: design that uses an uploaded font, store the file on your server and have the lookup return that address.
94: 
95: ### Google Fonts from your own host
96: 
97: `fonts.cssUrl` returns the stylesheet address for one face. Use it to serve Google families from your own server:
98: 
99: ```ts
100: configureRichText({

1: # Character styles
2: 
3: Character styles are the font family, size, weight, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and color of the letters.
4: Your toolbar sets them with one command each. A command changes a whole text box when the box is only selected, or the
5: selected words while someone is editing the box, so a headline can have one word in another color or weight.
6: 
7: ## Call the commands
8: 
9: On Konva the commands are on the manager that [enableRichText](ref:enableRichText) returns. On a plain canvas they are
10: on the object that [createCanvasRichText](ref:createCanvasRichText) returns. The names and arguments are the same.
11: 
12: ```ts
13: // Konva
14: const rt = enableRichText(stage);
15: rt.manager.toggleBold();
16: rt.manager.setColor("#5E2DC1");
17: 
18: // Plain canvas
19: const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render });
20: rt.toggleBold();
21: rt.setColor("#5E2DC1");
22: ```
23: 
24: The rest of this page shows the Konva calls. On a plain canvas, call the same commands on `rt`.
25: 
26: ## What a command changes
27: 
28: - **A selected box that is not being edited:** all of its text.
29: - **A box being edited, with words selected:** the selected words.
30: - **A box being edited, with only the cursor:** the whole paragraph the cursor is in. There is no style waiting for the
31:   next letters typed: new letters take the style of the letter before the cursor.
32: - **Boxes you name:** every command takes an optional last argument, a list of boxes. The command then changes those
33:   boxes instead of the selection. A box in the list that is being edited still changes only its selected words.
34: 
35: ```ts
36: rt.manager.setColor("#FF7903", [headline, footer]);
37: ```
38: 
39: Each command is one undo step, and a command on several boxes is one undo step for all of them. A paragraph whose
40: letters are all changed also takes the new family, size, weight or color as its own, so text typed later in it, and an
41: empty line in it, use that style.
42: 
43: ## Font family
44: 
45: ```ts
46: await rt.manager.setFontFamily("Lora");
47: ```
48: 
49: `setFontFamily` returns a promise. The library loads the family's regular, bold, italic and bold italic faces first,
50: then changes the text and lays it out in the new font. Until then the box keeps showing its current font, never a blank
51: box. Bold, italic and the weight already set are kept. On several boxes, every box's font loads first and then all of
52: them change together, as one undo step.
53: 
54: Every [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com) family works by name. For your own fonts, pass their address as the
55: third argument, after the boxes (`null` for the current box):
56: 
57: ```ts
58: await rt.manager.setFontFamily("Acme Sans", null, {
59:   fontFaceUrl: "https://cdn.example.com/acme-sans.css", // a stylesheet with the family's @font-face rules
60:   fontImageUrl: "https://cdn.example.com/acme-sans.png", // a preview image for your font picker
61:   description: "Rounded sans for headlines",
62:   attribution: "Acme Type Foundry",
63: });
64: ```
65: 
66: | Option | What it does |
67: | --- | --- |
68: | `fontFaceUrl` | The address of a stylesheet with the family's `@font-face` rules. The library loads the font from it and saves the address in the document, so the design opens anywhere without your fonts lookup. |
69: | `fontImageUrl` | The address of a preview image of the font. Saved with the font; never drawn. |
70: | `description` | A short description of the font. Saved with the font; never drawn. |
71: | `attribution` | The font's author or license credit. Saved with the font; never drawn. |
72: 
73: The three descriptive fields are saved only for a custom font: one given a `fontFaceUrl`, or one your fonts lookup
74: knows. A family your lookup knows needs no options at all, and its address is saved the same way. The plain canvas
75: takes the same options: `rt.setFontFamily(family, null, options)`. Both ways are described in [Fonts](fonts).
76: 
77: ## Font size
78: 
79: ```ts
80: rt.manager.setFontSize(48); // every changed letter is 48 pixels
81: rt.manager.scaleFontSize(1.15); // every size 15% larger, in proportion
82: ```
83: 
84: `setFontSize` gives every changed letter one size, in pixels. `scaleFontSize` multiplies each letter's own size by a
85: factor, so mixed sizes keep their proportions. In "Saturday, 10am - 4pm" with "Saturday" larger, scaling by 1.15 makes
86: both parts larger and "Saturday" stays the larger word. Outline widths scale with the letters, and so does the letter
87: spacing of every paragraph changed whole. Line height and paragraph spacing are multiples of the font size, so they
88: follow on their own. A factor of 1, zero, a negative number or `NaN` changes nothing.
89: 
90: On a box that is not being edited, `scaleFontSize` scales the whole box: every size, the letter spacing, the outlines,
91: paragraph borders and the drop shadow.
92: 
93: > **Tip:** Inside a scaled Konva group, sizes, outline widths and letter spacing are read and set as they look on
94: > screen. A size read from the toolbar state, changed and written back moves by exactly the change.
95: 
96: ## Font weight
97: 
98: ```ts
99: rt.manager.setFontWeight(600); // 100 to 900
100: ```

1: # Paragraphs
2: 
3: Paragraph settings are alignment, line height, the space after a paragraph and letter spacing. They belong to a whole
4: paragraph, never to a few words, so a command changes every paragraph it reaches from start to end. Your toolbar sets
5: each one with a single command.
6: 
7: ## Call the commands
8: 
9: ```ts
10: // Konva: const rt = enableRichText(stage)
11: rt.manager.setAlignment("center");
12: rt.manager.setLineHeight(1.3);
13: rt.manager.setParagraphSpacing(0.5);
14: rt.manager.setLetterSpacing(1);
15: 
16: // Plain canvas: const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render })
17: rt.setAlignment("center");
18: ```
19: 
20: The commands have the same names and arguments on both surfaces. The rest of this page shows the Konva calls.
21: 
22: ## Which paragraphs change
23: 
24: - **A selected box that is not being edited:** every paragraph in the box.
25: - **A box being edited, with text selected:** every paragraph the selection touches, each one whole.
26: - **A box being edited, with only the cursor:** the paragraph the cursor is in. A cursor at the end of a paragraph's
27:   text belongs to that paragraph.
28: - **Boxes you name:** pass a list of boxes as the optional last argument to change those boxes instead of the
29:   selection: `rt.manager.setAlignment("center", [headline, footer])`.
30: 
31: Each command is one undo step, also when it changes several boxes.
32: 
33: ## Alignment
34: 
35: ```ts
36: rt.manager.setAlignment("left"); // "left" | "center" | "right" | "justify"
37: ```
38: 
39: Alignment places each line of the paragraph in the box. `"justify"` spreads the spare width over the spaces of each
40: wrapped line, so both edges are straight; the paragraph's last line is set to the left. A line that fills the whole
41: width starts at the left edge whatever the alignment.
42: 
43: A list's markers follow the alignment of their items. A line laid out by tab stops ignores alignment and is never
44: justified: see [Tab stops](tabs).
45: 
46: ## Line height
47: 
48: ```ts
49: rt.manager.setLineHeight(1.2); // a multiple of the font size
50: ```
51: 
52: Line height is a multiple of the font size: `1.2` makes each line 120% of its size. Each line takes its height from the
53: largest letters on it, so a bigger word makes only its own line taller. New text made with `createDocumentFromText` has a
54: line height of 1.4.
55: 
56: ## Space after a paragraph
57: 
58: ```ts
59: rt.manager.setParagraphSpacing(0.5); // half the font size after each paragraph
60: ```
61: 
62: Paragraph spacing is the space after a paragraph, as a multiple of that paragraph's font size: `0` is none and `1` is
63: one font size. It is added below every paragraph except the last one, so it never makes the box taller below the last
64: line. A soft line break (Shift+Enter) stays inside the paragraph and adds no paragraph spacing. New text has a
65: paragraph spacing of 0.5.
66: 
67: ## Letter spacing
68: 
69: ```ts
70: rt.manager.setLetterSpacing(2); // 2 pixels after every letter
71: ```
72: 
73: Letter spacing is extra space after every letter, in pixels. `0` is the font's normal spacing, and a negative value
74: tightens the letters. The value is a length, not a multiple, so `setFontSize` doesn't change it; `scaleFontSize` scales
75: it along with the letters.
76: 
77: > **Note:** Letter spacing belongs to the paragraph, like alignment. Selecting a few words and setting letter spacing
78: > changes the whole paragraphs those words are in. A run of text has no letter spacing of its own: a document that
79: > gives a run one has it removed when the document loads.
80: 
81: Inside a scaled Konva group, letter spacing is read and set in pixels as it looks on screen, the same as font sizes.
82: 
83: ## In the document
84: 
85: Each paragraph keeps these settings in its `blockAttributes`:
86: 
87: ```json
88: {
89:   "alignment": "center",
90:   "lineHeight": 1.4,
91:   "paragraphSpacing": 0.5,
92:   "letterSpacing": 0
93: }
94: ```
95: 
96: [FormattingState](ref:FormattingState) reports the settings of the paragraph the cursor is in (or of the first
97: paragraph, for a box that is only selected) as `alignment`, `lineHeight`, `paragraphSpacing` and `letterSpacing`.
98: 
99: ## In the API reference
100:

1: # Lists
2: 
3: A list item is a paragraph with a marker in front of it. The marker can be a bullet, a number, any character such as a
4: symbol, a letter or an emoji, or a vector shape with a mark inside it, such as a white check in a colored circle. Lists
5: are for menus, feature lists and steps, and people edit them with the keys they already know.
6: 
7: ## Make a list
8: 
9: ```ts
10: // Konva: const rt = enableRichText(stage)
11: rt.manager.toggleBulletList(); // bullets, with the default "disc" marker
12: rt.manager.toggleBulletList("★"); // bullets, with a star
13: 
14: // Plain canvas: const rt = createCanvasRichText({ onChange: render })
15: rt.toggleBulletList();
16: ```
17: 
18: `toggleBulletList` turns the paragraphs it reaches into list items, or back into plain paragraphs. If any of them is
19: not a list item yet, all of them become list items, and the ones that were list items already keep their marker. If
20: all of them are list items, all of them become plain paragraphs, and their marker, indent and marker offset are removed.
21: 
22: It reaches paragraphs the same way the paragraph commands do: every paragraph of a box that is only selected, every
23: paragraph the selection touches while editing, or the paragraph the cursor is in. To change boxes you name instead,
24: pass them as the optional last argument. With no marker to give, pass `undefined` first:
25: 
26: ```ts
27: rt.manager.toggleBulletList(undefined, [specials]);
28: ```
29: 
30: Each call is one undo step.
31: 
32: ## Change the marker
33: 
34: ```ts
35: rt.manager.setBulletStyle("decimal"); // 1. 2. 3.
36: rt.manager.setBulletStyle("🍋"); // an emoji, drawn in color
37: ```
38: 
39: `setBulletStyle` changes the marker of the list items it reaches and leaves plain paragraphs as they are. The marker is
40: one of these:
41: 
42: | Marker | Draws |
43: | --- | --- |
44: | `"disc"` | • (the default) |
45: | `"circle"` | ◦ |
46: | `"square"` | ▪ |
47: | `"decimal"` | 1. 2. 3. |
48: | Any character | That character: `"–"`, `"➤"`, `"★"`, `"✓"`, a letter, or an emoji |
49: 
50: Numbers count the list items that follow one another: a plain paragraph, or an item with a different marker, between
51: two numbered items starts the count again at 1.
52: 
53: A character marker is drawn in the font, size and color of its item's first letter, at the regular weight. Under a
54: gradient or image fill, a character marker takes the fill as the letters do.
55: 
56: > **Limit:** A marker is one character. A string longer than three UTF-16 code units, such as some emoji made of
57: > several joined emoji, draws a disc instead.
58: 
59: ## A shape with a mark inside
60: 
61: A vector marker is drawn from two shapes, each in its own color: a backing shape and a mark on top of it. Set it as
62: `marker` in each list item's `blockAttributes`, then apply the document with `setDocument`, which is one undo step:
63: 
64: ```ts
65: // A check mark in a 24x24 box (SVG path data)
66: const CHECK = "M9 16.2 4.8 12l-1.4 1.4L9 19 21 7l-1.4-1.4L9 16.2z";
67: 
68: const doc = structuredClone(box.getDocument()); // never change the live document in place
69: for (const block of doc.blocks) {
70:   if (block.type === "list-item") {
71:     block.blockAttributes.marker = { shape: "circle", shapeFill: "#5E2DC1", glyphPath: CHECK, glyphColor: "#FFFFFF" };
72:   }
73: }
74: rt.manager.setDocument(doc, [box]); // plain canvas: rt.setDocument(doc, [box])
75: ```
76: 
77: | Field | What it does |
78: | --- | --- |
79: | `shape` | The backing shape: `"circle"`, `"square"` (a square with rounded corners), or `"none"` (the default) for the mark alone. |
80: | `shapeFill` | The backing shape's color, any CSS color. Default: the item's text color. |
81: | `glyphPath` | The mark, as SVG path data in a 24x24 box. The path is filled, not stroked. On a backing shape the mark takes 60% of the marker's size. Leave it out for a shape with no mark. |
82: | `glyphColor` | The mark's color. Default: the item's text color. |
83: | `scale` | The marker's size, as a multiple of the item's font size. Default 1. |
84: 
85: A vector marker is centered in the space before the item's text, at the middle of the capital letters' height. It keeps
86: its own colors under a gradient or image fill. `setBulletStyle` replaces a vector marker with the character you give
87: it.
88: 
89: ## Indent
90: 
91: Two list settings in `blockAttributes` place the marker and the text, both as multiples of the item's font size:
92: 
93: | Field | What it does |
94: | --- | --- |
95: | `listIndent` | Where the item's text starts, from the left edge of the box. Default 2. Every line of the item starts there, so wrapped lines line up with the first. |
96: | `bulletOffset` | Where the marker's space starts, from the left edge of the box. Default 0.6. The marker is centered between this and `listIndent`. |
97: 
98: There is no command for these two settings: set them in the document and apply it with `setDocument`, as for a vector
99: marker. Because they are multiples of the font size, the indent grows and shrinks with the text.
100:

1: # Resize handles
2: 
3: A text box has a width, and its height follows the text. People resize a box with handles: a side handle changes the
4: width and the text rewraps, and a corner handle scales the text itself. A side handle never makes the box narrower
5: than its longest word. On Konva the handles are your own `Konva.Transformer`; on a plain canvas the library draws
6: them.
7: 
8: ## What each handle does
9: 
10: | Handle | What changes | Limit |
11: | --- | --- | --- |
12: | Left or right side | The width. The text rewraps at the new width. | Never narrower than the longest word |
13: | Corner | The type, in proportion: font sizes, outline widths, letter spacing and the shadow scale together, and the width with them | At least 20 pixels wide and 20 tall |
14: 
15: - Hold Alt while dragging to resize about the box's center instead of the opposite side or corner.
16: - A box has no top or bottom side handle, because stretching type vertically would distort it.
17: - A curved box has corner handles only: its width does not change the curve.
18: - A corner drag scales the font sizes in the document. The box is never left scaled, so text stays sharp and a
19:   48-pixel headline scaled to double reads as 96 in your toolbar.
20: - Each resize is one undo step.
21: 
22: ## Set the width from code
23: 
24: ```ts
25: // Konva
26: headline.width(320);
27: 
28: // Plain canvas
29: headline.setWidth(320);
30: ```
31: 
32: The text rewraps at the new width. If one word is wider than the width you set, the box widens to fit that word.
33: `getLongestWordWidth()` returns that width in pixels, if you want to use it as your own minimum:
34: 
35: ```ts
36: const narrowest = headline.getLongestWordWidth();
37: ```
38: 
39: ## Konva: your transformer
40: 
41: [enableRichText](ref:enableRichText) uses your transformer. Attach it to a box the way you attach it to any node; the
42: library sets which handles the box offers and handles the drag:
43: 
44: ```ts
45: const selection = new Konva.Transformer();
46: layer.add(selection);
47: const rt = enableRichText(stage);
48: 
49: stage.on("mousedown", (e) => {
50:   if (e.target instanceof RichText) selection.nodes([e.target]);
51:   else if (e.target === stage) selection.nodes([]);
52: });
53: ```
54: 
55: By default any `Konva.Transformer` on the stage is the selection transformer. If your stage has several, name yours
56: with a selector: `enableRichText(stage, { transformers: { selection: "#selection", groupChild: "#inGroup" } })`.
57: `groupChild` is the transformer for a box selected inside a group; a flat box in a group offers its side handles only,
58: and a curved one none (the group's own handles scale it).
59: 
60: To ungroup, move each box out before you destroy the group, or `group.destroy()` destroys the boxes with it. Keep
61: where it is on screen with `absolutePosition()` and `getAbsoluteRotation()`, then call
62: `box.bakeScale(group.scaleX(), group.scaleY())` so the group's scale goes into the type instead of staying on the
63: node. A box you move stays editable; enableRichText follows it.
64: 
65: With several boxes in one transformer, a corner drag scales each box's type and keeps each box centered where the
66: transformer put it; a side drag changes each box's width.
67: 
68: Each box fires `richtext:transformStart` and `richtext:transformEnd` when a resize with the transformer starts and
69: ends. The event's `target` is the box:
70: 
71: ```ts
72: headline.on("richtext:transformEnd", (e) => saveBox(e.target)); // e.target: the box
73: ```
74: 
75: ### A box without enableRichText
76: 
77: A `RichText` handles its own transforms by default. Give it a transformer, or settings for one it makes:
78: 
79: ```ts
80: const box = new RichText({ x: 40, y: 40, width: 400, document: doc, transformer: myTransformer });
81: 
82: const other = new RichText({ x: 40, y: 200, width: 400, document: doc, transformerConfig: { anchorSize: 10 } });
83: layer.add(other.getTransformer()!); // the transformer it made: add it to a layer yourself
84: ```
85: 
86: To leave transforms to Konva's own scaling, pass `autoHandleTransforms: false`.
87: 
88: ### Scaling from code
89: 
90: | Method | Does |
91: | --- | --- |
92: | `box.bakeScale(scaleX, scaleY)` | Moves the node's Konva scale into the type: font sizes scale by `scaleY`, the width by `scaleX`, and the node's scale goes back to 1. For your own transform code. |
93: | `box.resize(pageScaleX, pageScaleY)` | Fits the box to a page drawn at a new scale: its position scales by each factor, its type and width by the smaller one. |
94: 
95: ## Plain canvas: built-in handles
96: 
97: [createCanvasRichText](ref:createCanvasRichText) draws the selected box's outline and handles in `rt.paintOverlay(ctx)`.
98: A click selects the box under it, a second click edits it, a drag moves it, and the handles resize it by the rules
99: above. Each move and resize is one undo step.
100:

1: # Keyboard and mouse
2: 
3: Text boxes respond to the keys and gestures people already know from word processors: typing, moving the cursor,
4: selecting with the mouse or Shift, copy and paste, undo and the right-click menu. All of these work with no code once
5: you call `enableRichText` or `createCanvasRichText`. This page lists every key and gesture, says which keys the library
6: leaves to your app, and shows the commands that do the same from your own buttons and menus.
7: 
8: ## Start and stop editing
9: 
10: A box is first selected, then edited:
11: 
12: 1. Click a box to select it. On Konva your app selects it, by putting it on your `Konva.Transformer`. On a plain
13:    canvas the built-in object controls select it (or your app calls `rt.select(box)` when `objectControls` is off).
14: 2. Click the selected box again to place the cursor and type.
15: 
16: Editing ends when someone presses Esc (the box stays selected), presses anywhere outside the box being edited, or
17: starts resizing the box with a handle. Clicks on your page outside the canvas, such as on your toolbar, do not end
18: editing.
19: 
20: From your code:
21: 
22: ```ts
23: // Konva
24: rt.manager.edit(box);      // start editing the box now, as a click on the selected box would
25: rt.manager.stopEditing();  // stop editing; the box stays selected
26: rt.manager.editing();      // the box being edited, or null
27: isEditingText();           // is any box on the page being edited?
28: stopEditingText();         // stop editing wherever it is on the page
29: 
30: // Plain canvas
31: rt.stopEditing();
32: rt.editing();
33: ```
34: 
35: `isEditingText` and `stopEditingText` are exported from `@mycreativeshop/rich-text/konva`. A box marked `editable: false`
36: never starts editing; see the read-only boxes section of [Getting started](getting-started).
37: 
38: ## Keys
39: 
40: Keys reach the text only while a box is being edited. "Ctrl" means Ctrl or Cmd: both work on every system.
41: 
42: **Typing**
43: 
44: | Key | What it does |
45: | --- | --- |
46: | Any character | Types it, in the style of the letter before the cursor, or of the first selected letter |
47: | Enter | Starts a new paragraph in the same style. In an empty list item, Enter ends the list |
48: | Shift+Enter | A line break inside the paragraph |
49: | Tab | Types a tab: the text after it moves to the paragraph's next tab stop (see [Tab stops](tabs)) |
50: | Backspace, Delete | Deletes the letter before or after the cursor, or the selection |
51: 
52: **Moving and selecting**
53: 
54: | Key | What it does |
55: | --- | --- |
56: | Left, Right | Moves the cursor one letter; with Shift, extends the selection |
57: | Up, Down | Moves the cursor one line; with Shift, extends the selection |
58: | Home, End | Moves the cursor to the start or end of the line; with Shift, extends the selection |
59: | Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End | Moves the cursor to the start or end of the text; with Shift, extends the selection |
60: | Ctrl+A | Selects all of the box's text |
61: | Esc | Stops editing; the box stays selected |
62: 
63: **Clipboard and undo**
64: 
65: | Key | What it does |
66: | --- | --- |
67: | Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X | Copies or cuts the selection, with its styles |
68: | Ctrl+V | Pastes at the cursor, replacing the selection |
69: | Ctrl+Z | Undo |
70: | Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y | Redo |
71: | Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U | Left to your app (see below) |
72: 
73: ## Mouse and touch
74: 
75: | Gesture | What it does |
76: | --- | --- |
77: | Click | Selects a box; a click on the selected box places the cursor |
78: | Drag across text | Selects text in the box being edited, also past the box's edge |
79: | Drag a box | Moves it: on Konva when the box is `draggable`, on a plain canvas with the object controls. A box being edited does not move |
80: | Double-click | On the selected box or the box being edited, selects the word under the pointer |
81: | Shift+click | Extends the selection to the click |
82: | Right-click | Opens the menu: spelling suggestions, Cut, Copy and Paste |
83: | Side handles | Change the width; the text wraps again (see [Resize handles](box)) |
84: | Corner handles | Scale the text |
85: 
86: On touch screens a tap is a click, and a double-tap selects a word. The library allows a little more movement and time
87: for a touch than for a mouse before a tap counts as a drag or two taps stop counting as a double-tap.
88: 
89: ## Bold, italic and underline keys
90: 
91: The library does not bind Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I or Ctrl+U, because what they do belongs to your app's toolbar. While a box is
92: being edited, a Ctrl+letter key the library does not use never types its letter, and the key goes on to your page.
93: Bind the keys yourself:
94: 
95: ```ts
96: window.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
97:   if (!(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) || e.altKey) return;
98:   const commands = rt.manager; // plain canvas: rt
99:   if (!commands.selected()) return; // no box selected: the key is the browser's
100:   const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
